lines: Thank you for keeping me with you. A short road feels longer when the night has <shake>teeth</shake>.
You brought me through that trip safely. That turns a long road into a remembered kindness.
I am still here in one piece, and that matters more than I can say <pulse>neatly</pulse>.
The road could have gone worse. It did not, and I know who helped with that.
I was not sure what waited out there, but you made sure I came home.
Safe steps are easy to forget until someone gives them to you.
I will remember that you did not leave me behind.
A journey feels different when someone is watching your back.
I came home with my breath steady. That is worth thanking you for.
You made a hard road feel possible, and I will not forget it.
I came back in one piece. That is the kind of help people remember.
You brought me through that trip safely. That turns a long road into a remembered kindness.
I am still here in one piece, and that matters more than I can say neatly.
The road was long, but it did not break us.
You kept your word well enough for me to stand here and say so.
There is comfort in arriving with nothing worse than tired feet.
I trusted you for that journey, and you gave me reason to be glad I did.
A safe return is not a small thing, not out there.
I know better than to take a quiet road for granted.
You saw me through. That matters.
I made it back, but not cleanly. Next time, we move slower or fight sooner.
I am still feeling that road. Do not mistake thanks for <italic>forgetting</italic>.
I returned, but the road left bruises in the story.
I am grateful to be home, but I would rather not pay that price twice.
The journey ended, but my ribs seem to be holding a meeting about it.
Next time, I would like fewer wounds between here and there.
I followed you through it, and I came back hurt. Both parts matter.
A safe ending does not erase a rough middle.
I am standing, yes, but do not call that the same as unharmed.
We made it through. Let us make better choices before we need to do that again.
You asked me to follow, then turned your hand against me. That is not a small thing.
I followed because I thought you meant to protect me. Now I know to measure that <pulse>promise</pulse> twice.
Following you was trust. Being struck after that was a lesson I did not ask for.
A road is dangerous enough without the guide becoming part of the danger.
You made yourself the reason I should have stayed home.
I remember the hit more clearly than the road now. That should tell you enough.
Trust walks slowly after betrayal, if it walks at all.
You led me out there, then taught me to fear your hand.
I will think carefully before I follow you anywhere again.
What you broke was not only skin. Remember that.
The boat helped. I will admit, being carried home by water is easier on the knees.
Floating beat walking the whole way. I will admit that.
The boat did honest work carrying us along.
A boat underfoot makes a long road feel kinder.
I was glad for the water once it stopped looking so wide.
My legs thank you for choosing a boat.
That boat saved us time, trouble, and more than a few complaints from me.
The river carried its share, and I respect good help when I see it.
I prefer solid ground, but the boat made a fair argument.
If every journey had a boat for the worst stretch, I would complain less.
Crossing ocean by boat was a better idea than swimming it. Thank you for keeping me dry.
The ocean looked less <wavy>endless</wavy> with a boat under us. Thank you for that much.
A boat between me and the deep water was the correct kind of wisdom.
I have never trusted the ocean, but I trusted the boat enough.
The water was too wide for comfort, but the boat kept its promise.
I am grateful we crossed the ocean without asking my arms to do all the work.
A boat makes deep water feel less like a threat and more like a road.
The ocean stayed below us, which is where I prefer it.
I did not enjoy the crossing, but I enjoyed arriving dry.
Next time we cross water that wide, I will still vote for a boat.
I crossed ocean water without a boat and still made it through. Next time, please find wood before waves.
I made it across, but my bones still vote for boats next time.
Swimming the ocean was not bravery. It was a shortage of better planning.
I am proud we survived that, but I do not want practice.
The ocean is too large to treat like a puddle.
I have never missed a boat more than I did out there.
The waves kept asking if I was tired. I was.
I made it across, but every splash felt like an argument against the plan.
Next time, let the boat do the swimming.
I am glad to be dry now. I would like to stay that way.
The boat ride was the quiet part. Getting hurt before or after it spoiled the memory.
The water stayed calm. The rest of the journey did not.
I would remember the boat more kindly if the hurt had not come with it.
The boat helped, yes, but it did not make the whole trip gentle.
I sat in that boat hoping the worst was behind us. It was not.
Water carried us for a while. Pain carried the rest.
I can thank the boat and still be angry about the bruises.
The trip had one peaceful stretch, and then the road corrected that.
A boat can carry a body, but it cannot keep trouble from waiting on shore.
Next time, I would like the boat ride without the injury attached.
The ocean crossing by boat was manageable. The part where I got hurt was less impressive.
The water stayed calm. The rest of the journey did not.
I would remember the boat more kindly if the hurt had not come with it.
The ocean was not the worst part, which is saying something.
The boat kept me above water, but not away from trouble.
Crossing the ocean was frightening enough without adding bruises to it.
I was grateful for the boat and less grateful for what happened around it.
The deep water behaved better than the rest of the trip.
I came back hurt, but at least the ocean did not get to keep me.
Next time, let the boat be the most difficult part. That would be enough.
Swimming across ocean and coming home hurt is not an adventure I want repeated.
Ocean swimming while hurt is a memory I would like to leave behind.
The <wavy>waves</wavy> did not help the bruises. Neither did the plan.
I had enough trouble staying above water without pain joining in.
That crossing asked too much from a body already having a bad day.
The ocean was wide, cold, and entirely too interested in my injuries.
I made it through, but that does not make it a good idea.
Next time, if I am hurt, we find a boat or we wait.
I still feel that journey when I move too quickly.
There are safer ways to cross water, and I would like to try one.
You put me in a boat, took me along, and then broke trust. Strange journey, worse ending.
Being carried over <wavy>water</wavy> did not make betrayal lighter.
The boat brought us along. You broke the part that mattered.
A calm ride does not excuse a cruel hand.
I remember the water, but I remember what you did more.
The boat carried me safely. You did not.
Trust should not sink after reaching shore.
I thought the water was the danger. I was wrong.
You made even that quiet boat ride feel foolish in hindsight.
Next time, I will think twice before sharing a boat with you.
Remember when you made me follow you across {follow_biome}? I still know that road by ache alone.
I remember {follow_biome}. Some places stay in your feet after you leave.
{follow_biome} was a long lesson in asking where we are going first.
I still think about {follow_biome} when my legs start complaining.
You led me through {follow_biome}, and I learned that scenery can be tiring.
{follow_biome} looked different once I had to cross it on foot.
I remember the sounds of {follow_biome} more than I expected.
Some paths through {follow_biome} feel longer after you have already walked them.
I know {follow_biome} better than I planned to.
Next time you mention {follow_biome}, I may sit down first.
Remember when you made me follow you over {follow_distance} blocks? My legs complained for days.
{follow_distance} blocks is a long way to wonder if you chose the right guide.
My legs remember those {follow_distance} blocks with unnecessary detail.
After {follow_distance} blocks, even flat ground starts feeling personal.
I learned exactly how long {follow_distance} blocks can feel when you are following someone.
{follow_distance} blocks gave me plenty of time to question your sense of direction.
I still think my feet should have been thanked after that walk.
There are shorter ways to build trust than dragging someone {follow_distance} blocks.
That walk made every bed in the village look like a miracle.
Next time we go that far, I am asking about the destination first.
Remember when you took me along in a boat? I was not sure whether to thank you or ask where the oars had gone.
I remember that boat. Sitting still while the world moved was strange comfort.
The oars had a plan. I wish the rest of us had one too.
That boat trip was quieter than walking, which I appreciated.
I still remember watching the shore move like it had somewhere to be.
A boat is a strange thing. You sit, and somehow distance happens.
I was glad for the boat, even if I pretended not to be nervous.
The water carried us, and for once my feet were not responsible.
I remember wondering if boats always sound that uncertain.
If nothing else, that boat gave my legs a fine argument for resting.
Remember when you took me across ocean water without a boat? I remember every splash.
No boat, ocean water, and too much time to think. I remember.
I still remember the ocean trying to make every step impossible.
The ocean is much larger when you are inside it.
I learned that day that waves have no manners.
Crossing ocean water without a boat is not something I recommend.
I remember looking for shore and finding more water instead.
Every wave seemed to ask why we had no boat. I had no answer.
I still feel tired when I think about that crossing.
Next time the ocean is involved, I would like wood beneath me.
That boat trip was part of a {follow_distance} block outing. Water did some of the work, but not enough.
That boat helped with {follow_distance} blocks of trouble, but not enough to make it easy.
{follow_distance} blocks sounds shorter when water does some of the carrying.
Even with a boat, {follow_distance} blocks is a long way to follow someone.
The boat spared my feet for a while, then the road asked for payment anyway.
I appreciated the boat more with every block after it ended.
{follow_distance} blocks is still {follow_distance} blocks, even with a floating shortcut.
The boat made part of the trip peaceful. The rest made up for it.
Water carried us for some of those blocks, and I thank it for its service.
Next time we travel that far, I want to know how much of it floats.
Remember when I followed you and you hit me? I do. Still hurts.
I followed because I thought you meant safety. The hit changed that sentence.
Some memories hurt before anyone says another word.
I remember trusting you on that road. I remember regretting it.
You made following you feel like a mistake.
That kind of hurt stays longer than the bruise.
I learned something about your promises that day.
Being led somewhere and then struck is not easy to forget.
I can still hear the part of me that should have turned back.
If you wonder why I hesitate, remember what you taught me.
I remember following you home hurt. I was grateful, but not exactly comfortable.
I was grateful to get home and angry that getting home hurt. Both fit.
That journey ended here, but the ache took longer to arrive.
I remember each step better than I wanted to.
Getting home mattered. Getting hurt on the way mattered too.
I tried not to slow us down, but pain has its own pace.
That road felt longer once I was limping through it.
I was glad to see the village again, even through the hurt.
A safe return can still leave a sore memory.
Next time, I would rather arrive without counting every bruise.
It held when trouble came close. That matters more than shine.
I had to trust it in a fight. I am glad you thought ahead.
The {gear_kind} earned its place. I noticed that more than I expected.
When it mattered, I was better prepared than I would have been alone.
Good gear makes fear easier to carry.
The {gear_kind} did what it needed to do when the moment turned sharp.
I will not pretend I was fearless, but I was ready.
That {gear_kind} made the difference between panic and action.
It is one thing to be given gear. It is another for it to hold under pressure.
I trust the {gear_kind} more now. It proved itself when it counted.
